  WHY: A `Refs #N` mention can cause cleanup to remove an unrelated blocked-state gate; the reviewers differ on severity, and the higher severity is used.

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/provider_outage.py: `referenced_issues()` (lines 433–436), its use at line 718, and issue cleanup at lines 753–761 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Resume cleanup treats every `#N` in a PR title or body as a linked issue.
  WHY: A PR that says `Refs #N` can add issue N to the cleanup set even when it did not cause N to be blocked; if the latest `ai:review-blocked` label event on N was made by the workflow account during the outage window, cleanup removes that label and clears an unrelated blocked-state gate.
- scripts/provider_outage.py: `resume_attempts()` (lines 279–285), attempt calculation at line 821, resume-comment POST at lines 859–860, and error handling at lines 805–810 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The resume-attempt limit is counted only from successfully posted resume comments.
  WHY: If resume actions run but posting the resume comment fails, the error is caught and the tick returns with `skip_review_dispatch` still true; no attempt or handled keys are persisted, so the next tick repeats the actions with the same attempt number and the sweep remains paused indefinitely.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh: `provider_outage_record()` (lines 218–224) and the `provider_unavailable` branch (lines 234–245) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: A missing outage helper or failed `record` call is swallowed, after which the intake exits successfully.
  WHY: The first provider-outage report can finish without creating a marker or sending the outage alert; the intake failure notification does not run because the branch exits with status 0, and without a marker the probe cannot pause the sweep or resume the affected reviews.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- scripts/provider_outage.py: referenced_issues() (lines 433-436), its use in resume_repo() (line 718: `referenced.update(referenced_issues(pr))`), and the referenced-issue cleanup loop (lines 755-763) with _remove_outage_label() (lines 766-782) | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Resume cleanup treats every `#N` mention in a paused PR's title or body as a linked issue whose `ai:review-blocked` label may be removed.
  WHY: During an outage window, a PR that fails for a genuine non-provider reason can label its linked issues `ai:review-blocked`; if such a labelled issue number appears as `Refs #N` in a resume-candidate PR body, recovery removes that label and clears a real blocked-state gate.
- scripts/provider_outage.py: resume_attempts() (lines 279-285, counts only successfully posted resume comments), the resume-comment POST in _resume() (lines 859-860), and tick()'s catch-all (lines 805-810); MAX_RESUME_ATTEMPTS at line 134 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The resume-attempt cap is derived exclusively from resume comments that were successfully posted.
  WHY: If the resume-comment POST fails, tick() catches the error and keeps the marker open without recording an attempt or handled keys; subsequent ticks re-run resume and re-dispatch the same PRs indefinitely, bypassing the documented attempt-cap invariant.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh: provider_outage_record() (lines 211-232: helper missing or failed `record` call is logged and returns 0) and the provider_unavailable branch (lines 234-246: exits 0 with no marker and no alert) | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A failed outage record call is logged and swallowed, with no marker or Telegram fallback alert.
  WHY: With no marker, the probe cannot discover the outage and the sweep keeps spending review runs on a dead provider; persistent record failure leaves the marker path silently off.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
